in_sanskrit.name: पराशुराम
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: परा (above) आशु (swift) राम (Rama) । Rama who wields an axe above his head.

in_hindi.name: पराशुराम
in_hindi.long_meaning: परा (above) शु (swift) राम (Rama) । राम जिसका पाँव पर पराशु होता है

in_telugu.name: పరాశురామ్

He is considered the patron god of the martial community of Kerala, who have been practicing the martial art of Kalaripayattu for over 3000 years. The festival of Thiruvathira celebrates Parashuram's defeat of theAsura king, Mahishasura, and also pays homage to Parashuram, who is considered a male god and a symbol of masculine power.

It also highlights the idea of sattvic (pure) rage, where anger is used in the pursuit of justice and righteousness, rather than being a destructive force. Additionally, Parashuram's association with Lord Shiva, who bestowed him with an axe, symbolizes the power of the divine in one's life, as well as the potential for transformation.
